get.description: What an SDK needs to open the pool: the versioned, immutable genesis file (fetch it once and cache it to a file), its sha256, a minisign signature and the public key to verify it with, and the read-only HTTPS ledger proxy for networks that block Indy client ports.

post.description: Attributes are strings on the wire (no nested values, no native numbers). `expiresAt` (epoch seconds) is mandatory: v1 has no revocation, so every credential carries an expiry that every proof request checks.

post.summary: Deprecate or reactivate a schema version
post.description: A deprecated version refuses new offers; credentials already issued under it stay verifiable and templates with `versions: "all"` keep accepting them.
Published without revocation support (v1 decision, cannot be changed later for this definition).

Returns an out-of-band invitation URL for the holder app to open or scan (encode the URL in a QR code). `multiUse: true` serves kiosk and web-embed cases where many wallets connect through one invitation.

Asynchronous. Returns the exchange immediately in state `offer-sent`; `credential-issued` means the holder received it, `done` that it acknowledged. Attribute values are strings; `expiresAt` is epoch seconds as a string and must be in the future. `credentialDefinitionId` accepts the catalogue id or the ledger id.

Asynchronous. Either a stored `templateId` or an inline `request` in the template shape. Every group automatically checks `expiresAt >= now`. When the exchange reaches `done`, `verified` and the `disclosed` attributes are available.

Each group discloses attributes from one credential and may add integer predicates. Credentials are referenced by schema name (all versions, or active only) or by credential definition id. `expiresAt` is always predicated and can never be disclosed.

One wallet per SDK installation. The returned `walletToken` is shown once; pass it to your app, which gives it to the SDK. The platform never learns who the end user is; `externalId` is your own reference and is echoed in `wallet.sync_requested` webhooks.

delete.description: Revokes the wallet token; the device keeps its local data and its mediator connection, but the platform stops mapping mediator webhooks to it.

put.description: One endpoint per tenant. The signing `secret` is returned only when it is created or rotated. Events are POSTed as `{ id, type, createdAt, tenantId, data }` with `X-12id-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<t>.<body>")>`. Answer 2xx within 10 s; failures are retried with exponential backoff (about 12 attempts over a day) and then dead-lettered.
